problem: Prove that every Poisson–binomial law with variance V ≥ 1 satisfies a variance-scaled lower bound V δD ≥ 1/4 on its normalized Turán deficit at the first descent.
debate: The study of log-concavity and Turán-type inequalities for discrete probability distributions, including ultra-log-concavity bounds of Hillion and Johnson, bounds of Johnson and Dümbgen–Wellner, and Darroch's modal-location theorem.
gap: All existing lower bounds on the deficit δk (from ultra-log-concavity, Johnson, Dümbgen–Wellner, or Pitman) depend on n, success probabilities, or k alone and degenerate when summands with pi near 0 or 1 accumulate at fixed variance; no variance-scaled bound existed.
contribution: Proves V δD ≥ 1/4 with best constant between 1/4 and 1/3, extends to δk ≥ 1/(4V + |k − D|) everywhere, bounds curvature at the rightmost mode as 1/(4V + 1) ≤ δc < 2/V, and applies to Haar unitary matrices showing 1/log N order versus 1/N from ultra-log-concavity.
note: Clear problem, genuine variance-scaled contribution, explicit bounds with tight range; advance for review.
